results.notes: Study 1, individual randomization, final idea, round all; no randomized-order crossover or first-round record. Use all 486 rows of data_clean.csv with unique participant_id, including page_visit_only rows. The file is already the final analyzed sample: the paper (PDF p. 7, section 4.3) reports 16 exclusions from 502 recruited (10 attention checks, 2 unauthorized AI use, 2 nonsense, 1 duplicate, 1 incomplete). The excluded raw rows are not supplied here, so their individual exclusion decisions cannot be independently audited. No further exclusions. bot_type mapping: feedback=Question-mode, suggestion=Suggestion-mode, improvement=Model-led, vanilla=Vanilla, control=Control. Average and Idea_quality are identical and equal mean(Rater1..Rater4) rounded half up to two decimals for every participant. That posted outcome is recreated and used consistently; without this participant-level rounding the vanilla mean is 2.6934210526, whereas the posted outcome mean is 2.6961052632 and reproduces Table 2's 2.70. One final idea per participant; four expert ratings are averaged within that participant before computing any arm statistics. Counts, means and SDs are checked against Table 2 (PDF p. 12), and against data_group_summary.csv. Sources for the rating rule: PDF pp. 7 and 22. Table 3 (PDF p. 12) is checked using the five-arm OLS residual SD, df=481, and Holm adjustment of four right-tailed t-tests, following Analysis_Study.Rmd lines 469-512. The posted code defines the paper's d denominator as the five-arm residual SD. All listed paper statistics reproduce at printed precision. The new raw difference is treatment minus control. Its SE is from two-arm OLS(quality ~ intercept + treatment) with HC2, using one row per randomized person; it is also verified as sqrt(s_t^2/n_t+s_c^2/n_c). Reported arm SDs use n-1. No assignment clusters.
